answer: Given the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.\\ \\ We reduce $A$ to row-echelon form using elementary row operations: \\ \\ Apply $R_2 \to R_2 - R_1$ and $R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1$: \\ $A \sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix}$ \\ \\ Apply $R_3 \to R_3 - R_2$: \\ $A \sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ \\ \\ Since the last row is all zeros, the number of non-zero rows is 2. \\ Therefore, $\text{Rank}(A) = 2$.
proTip: Always check for identical or proportional rows after applying elementary operations to easily spot zero rows.
